t.why_t_lands: STEP's letters are the first parting of ruling 6 of 13 November 2026. On these rows, joined to an entry by their own pointed head form, the letters held back rows of the same word wherever v203 gave fewer letters than STEP's own rows carry (4,380 lines). Relay v211 reads from TBESH's own first and third columns which letters are one word and widens t so that no line holds back a letter of the same word as a letter v203 gave. So the letters now part only another word, as the ruling means them to

lists.why_b_lands: BDB's own entries are the second parting of ruling 6 of 13 November 2026. On a row joined to an entry by its own pointed head form, b does two things at a place. With a number, it puts BDB's entry into what the gate gathers from the key's rows for the place's numbers, so BDB's own rows that carry b and no number and name another entry are withheld there. With no number, the row itself is withheld where the entries gathered hold none of its own. So b on a joined row changes what BDB's rows do at rest, and ship 11 held it until it was counted (ask B of 20 November). Relay v212 counted it on the reading this page reads (a place asks its word's own key, and the gate gathers from every row of that key, before the pointing and the kinds hold any back): 3,927 flips of BDB's own rows, left to withheld, at 2,215 places. It settled two classes, and relay v218 reissues both lists with them: «forget» (n.fr.aa) off 27 lines, where it went the wrong way; the 231 lines under the keys that spell the preposition «to» with an ending land as given with l.aa.ab, BDB's own parting of the joined letter; 102 lines take H4480 and one line H7945. It holds nothing back, so b lands on every line that gives it (23 November 2026)
